notes: §1985:VI.6.23.3 SR4: "Integer-1 and integer-2 may be signed. Integer-1 must be positive.", read with §1985:III.2's "neither signed nor zero unless explicitly allowed". BindSetTo and BindSetUpDown call GateCobol85IndexAmount, which at 85 (row set-arithmetic-expression-2002 unavailable) asks Cobol85OperandForms.IsInteger with sign Positive for integer-1 and Any for integer-2; IsInteger refuses zero at every sign, a decimal point and a sign detached by a space, and the refusal is COBOL0900. Probes at 85: TO 0, -1 (the witness), +0, -0, ZERO, 1.0, 1.5, - 1, 2 + 1, and a list SET IX, IY TO 0 refused; TO +2 and 00004 run (02, 04); UP BY 0, -0, 1.0, 1.5 refused; UP BY -1, +2, DOWN BY 1 run (02); 18-digit integers compile; --std 2002 accepts TO 0, TO -1 and UP BY 0.

next.reason: 1985: 'Integer-1 and integer-2 may be signed. Integer-1 must be positive.' 2023 replaces both with arithmetic expressions (§2023:14.9.39.2: arithmetic-expression-1 in format 1, arithmetic-expression-2 in format 2), which may be signed, and states no positivity rule. §2023:14.9.39.4 GR2 and GR4 check the value only at run time, setting EC-RANGE-INDEX when it is 'outside the limit specified in General rule 2 of 13.18.38'. §2023:13.18.38.4 GR2 makes that range include 'occurrence number (1 - integer-2)'. SET idx TO 0 or TO -1, refused at compile time in 1985, compiles and can succeed.
